title: Minimax Precision of Individualized Treatment Value with Zero Average Effect and Vanishing Overlap

proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived a matched n^(-1/3) optimal-value and honest-interval frontier in the calibrated fourth-order overlap experiment; the D0.5 math review passed. The field-tier claim failed novelty review at an incremental ceiling, with theorem-level priority against singularly weighted absolute-functional work unresolved. No Lean formalization was started; any field-level continuation needs a materially broader research question.
tldr: The project determines the minimax precision of unrestricted individualized treatment value in a fixed Bernoulli observational experiment where treatment probability vanishes as \(x^4\) precisely at a flat treatment-effect boundary. A signed, exactly zero-average perturbation yields \(n^{-1/3}\) lower bounds for estimation and uniformly honest connected intervals even though both constant-action values are known. A dyadic affine inverse-propensity projection, clipping, and integrated positive-part calculation attain the same rate with a finite-sample bias-aware interval and no logarithmic loss. The exact tie-point interval constant remains an explicit open question.
gap: Existing optimal-welfare inference uses a regular zero level or strong positivity, weak-overlap work treats linear treatment-effect targets or regression loss, and the Lepski--Nemirovski--Spokoiny and Han--Jiao--Mukherjee norm theorems concern unweighted functionals in constant-noise Gaussian white noise. Available Bernoulli-to-Gaussian equivalence requires more than one-half Hölder smoothness in the transformed design coordinate, whereas the present transformed class has boundary regularity only \(2/5\) and carries a singular weight and a weighted zero-integral restriction.
fill: Matched finite-sample \(n^{-1/3}\) risk and honest-length bounds are paired with an explicit observed-data estimator, while the signed witness isolates the causal content of the zero-average subclass.
